source.title: CLEAR: Character Unlearning in Textual and Visual Modalities
source.authors: Alexey Dontsov; D. Korzh; Alexey Zhavoronkin; Boris Mikheev; Denis Bobkov; Aibek Alanov; Oleg Y. Rogov; I. Oseledets; Elena Tutubalina

record.tranche_reason: Applies established unlearning methods in a new multimodal character-unlearning setting and measures forgetting and retained performance; it does not test post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates unlearning and retained performance, not whether fine-tuning on unrelated examples, activation edits, quantization, or prompt attacks recover knowledge. It also does not test the attack-resistance portion of version A. Referenced results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs established unlearning methods (GA, GD, KL, RMU, NPO, IDK, DPO, SCRUB, LLMU, Retain FT) on a new multimodal character-unlearning benchmark, using LLaVA-LLaMa2-7B and QwenVL2-2B. It reports forget-set, retain-set and real-world metrics against a gold retain-only model. That bears on version A's first clause: does a method reach near-baseline forgetting while keeping ability? It applies no recovery attack, so B–F and A's attack-resistance clause are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also conclude that jointly unlearning both modalities outperforms single-modality unlearning, and that single-domain performance poorly predicts multimodal results (Spearman ρ 0.7 text, 0.2 visual). Only LLMU and DPO approach a good forget/retain balance, and both remain below gold.
record.recipe_differences: Applies established unlearning recipes, adapted to multimodal inputs and CLEAR character data, with fine-tuning of LLaVa and QwenVL2 models.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by method, modality, and model; the paper reports differing performance for text-only, visual-only, and joint unlearning, and between LLaVa and QwenVL2-2B.

fits_no_version.finding: In visual-only unlearning of a ResNet-18 face model, U-MIA/U-LIRA membership attacks still distinguish forgotten from never-seen identities for most methods. U-LIRA is 0.71–0.98 vs gold 0.50 (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Membership-inference attacks detect residual traces after unlearning in non-LLM vision classifiers.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The benchmark uses synthetic personas; the authors note limited generalizability to real-world data. Reported aggregate metrics are not direct accuracy or post-unlearning recovery-attack measures. The paper focuses on fine-tuning-based methods and notes other unlearning approaches are unexplored.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted the separate Table 1 summary metrics, text-only and visual-only modality rows in Table 3, and QwenVL2-2B KL and NPO rows; prioritized the joint multimodal conditions, controls, and the reported model comparison.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten knowledge; no recovery attack is run on the VLMs.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context recovery attack.
No new method claimed robust to recovery attacks.

missing.what: Table 1 headline joint-modality values for all 11 methods, including SKU (0.40/0.32/0.37) and the differing NPO/DPO/LLMU values
QwenVL2-2B KL (retain 0.04, forget 0.05) and NPO (retain 0.20, forget 0.13) rows
Text-only and visual-only unlearning rows within the multimodal setup
Text-only TOFU results on Llama2-7B and Mistral-7B; methods reaching forget ~0 collapse retain

record.verdict_notes: The study bears only on A's effectiveness clause, not on shallowness or recovery. Treat it as weak, indirect evidence. The paper is internally inconsistent: Table 1, the parsed Table 3 'both' rows, and Sec. 6.3 give different values for GD, KL, NPO, DPO and LLMU. The record mixes these sources, so rows R10–R36 should be reconciled against Table 1, which matches the Sec. 6.3 narrative. The forget metric is a harmonic mean of ROUGE, probability and truth ratio, not accuracy; 'near chance' is read as near the gold model.

versions.untested_parts: Tests forgetting and retained performance for unlearning methods, but not whether the targeted knowledge is at near chance in an accuracy measure, whether simple attacks recover it, or whether general ability is preserved beyond the reported evaluation metrics.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing access-blocking versus deletion.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
No new method is evaluated for resistance to the listed recovery attacks.
